## portcheck

See what's using your ports, find free ones, and free them up

### Synopsis

portcheck shows which processes own local ports, checks whether ports are
free, finds free ports, safely stops the process holding a port, and checks
ports on remote hosts.

Running 'portcheck <port>' is a shortcut for 'portcheck check <port>'.

```
portcheck [port...] [flags]
```

### Examples

```
  portcheck list --listening      # everything accepting connections
  portcheck 3000                  # is 3000 free? who holds it?
  portcheck free -n 3             # three free ports
  portcheck kill 8080             # stop whatever listens on 8080
```

### Options

```
  -h, --help                help for portcheck
      --json                shorthand for --output json
      --log-format string   log format: text or json (default "text")
      --no-color            disable colors (also honors NO_COLOR)
  -o, --output string       output format: table, plain, csv, json (default: table on a terminal, plain otherwise)
  -v, --verbose             log diagnostic details to stderr
```
